solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Military corps once manoeuvring at the front again

indicators.note: the shuffled word is placed at the front, ahead of the corps abbreviation
troops manoeuvring are moved about, so the letters of the word once are shuffled

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers who were once on manoeuvres find themselves back in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' turns ONCE into ENCO, and 'at the front' puts that ahead of RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout for a repeat performance means the same as asking for it once more.

clue.text: Convenience food mostly consumed by former wife with little money

parts.note: ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: the food word is eaten inside the money word

parts.note: pence are small coins, little money

indicators.note: all but the final letter is used

parts.note: one's diet is one's food

explanation.surface: A ready meal largely eaten by an ex-wife who is short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DIET to DIE, which is 'consumed by' PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing what is convenient rather than principled is acting from self-interested practicality.

clue.text: Propellers won't start for airline personnel

indicators.note: the first letter of the propeller word is missing

parts.note: a ship's screws are its propellers

explanation.surface: A plane whose propellers won't start strands the cabin staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' drops the first S of SCREWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight staff are the teams that work on an aircraft.

clue.text: Poet's description of 20 ac's wines

definitions.meaning: the poet J W Burgon called Petra 'a ... city half as old as time'
the two colours of wine besides white

explanation.surface: A poet describing the wines of the ancient city at 20 across.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is PETRA; the line 'a rose-red city half as old as time' is from J W Burgon's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink and claret wines, and Burgon's phrase for Petra's sandstone.

clue.text: No end of fossil fuel in SE area on the Channel?

indicators.note: the shortened fuel sits within the letters for the south-eastern region

parts.note: SE is read as S plus EAST, the eastern area of the country

indicators.note: the last letter of the fuel word is dropped

parts.note: coal is the classic fossil fuel

explanation.surface: A gloomy forecast that fossil fuel will run out in south-east England by the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' cuts COAL to COA, which goes 'in' S plus EAST. The question mark flags that the definition is a description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Land bordering the English Channel is shore country, so the phrase describes it by example.

clue.text: One cooking breakfast might have this urge

definitions.text: One cooking breakfast might have this
definitions.meaning: a fried breakfast cook may get yolk spattered over his front
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.definitionFit: Spattered yolk on a cook, and the phrasal verb meaning to encourage.

clue.text: Bird going over continent reported in one country

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the bird and continent pair is said aloud

parts.note: a crow followed by Asia, the bird going before the continent in a down answer

explanation.surface: A bird flying over a continent is spotted in one country.
explanation.walkthrough: CROW then ASIA, said aloud, sounds like the Balkan country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic republic is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Vehicle reverses into an animal — a feline

indicators.note: the turned vehicle goes inside the animal

parts.note: a goat is an animal

indicators.note: the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car backs into an animal, which turns out to be a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a traffic accident; 'reverses' turns the vehicle round and 'into' places it inside the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-haired breed is a type of domestic cat.

clue.text: One commanding the waves heartily to lift a swimmer

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting means reading upwards, backwards
only the heart is kept, the first and last letters going

parts.note: King Canute famously ordered the tide to retreat

explanation.surface: A ruler of the waves tries with all his heart to raise a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' keeps ANUT from CANUTE, and 'to lift' turns it upwards. Canute was the English king said to have commanded the tide to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: This large ocean fish is an example of a creature that swims.

clue.text: Fliers up on top of mountain come down in field

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers

indicators.note: the first letter of mountain is taken

parts.note: aircraft land when they come down

explanation.surface: Airmen fly over a mountain top and come down in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAF into FAR; 'top of' mountain gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricultural land is the open country of fields.

clue.text: Recruitment organisation's name suppressed by D notice?

definitions.text: Recruitment organisation's name suppressed by D notice?

parts.words: Recruitment organisation's name suppressed by D notice?
parts.note: a D notice is a British government request that newspapers suppress a story, so it gags the journalists; also the name of an old forcible naval recruiting band

explanation.walkthrough: A D notice (Defence notice) is a British government request to the newspapers not to publish something, so it suppresses the journalists as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval crews were once filled by gangs that forcibly enlisted men, so the term names a recruiting body.

clue.text: Newspaper article on promiscuous activity ultimately censored

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another comes after it
the final letter of the wild-party word is cut out

parts.note: an orgy is a bout of promiscuous behaviour
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece about an orgy that ended up being censored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately censored' trims ORGY to ORG, and the article AN goes 'on' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper serving as the mouthpiece of a party or group is called its organ.

clue.text: Biased right-winger concludes Democrat is almost wicked

indicators.note: the right-winger comes at the end of the assembly
all but the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: criminal behaviour is wicked
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A partisan Conservative declares his Democrat opponent pretty much a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CRIMINAL to CRIMINA; 'concludes' puts TORY last. Tory means a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating people unfairly on prejudice is being biased, a near synonym.

clue.text: Unit of soldiers in reserve

definitions.meaning: a body of troops sent off on separate duty
reserve as a noun means aloofness, emotional distance

explanation.definitionFit: A detached military body; also aloofness, like personal reserve.

clue.text: Stopped journalists covering final part of campaign

indicators.note: the journalists wrap around the letter picked from campaign

parts.note: ED for editor, twice over for the plural

indicators.note: only the closing letter of campaign is taken

explanation.surface: Reporters covering the end of an election campaign find it has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'journalists' gives two EDs; 'covering' wraps them around N, the 'final part of' campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past tenses for something brought to a close.

clue.text: Maybe lancers will keep order, having got in control

indicators.note: the dance holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the lancers is a kind of quadrille, so an example of a dance
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Lancers, those cavalrymen, keeping order having taken control.
explanation.walkthrough: The lancers is a nineteenth-century square dance, not cavalry here; 'will keep' holds the Order of Merit and the word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dominant is having the upper hand, power over others.

clue.text: Alternative vote leading to male revolutionary's downfall

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the alternative vote system
Alan is a man's name
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: Electoral reform brings about the political downfall of a male rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: AV (alternative vote) was the voting system put to a UK referendum in 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sweeping down a mountain is a literal downfall.

clue.text: American artillery shake up Asian city

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the pair is read upwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to stir is to shake up

explanation.surface: American guns shake up an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the gunners and the shaking together as one block, read from the bottom of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Punjab city of the Golden Temple is in India.

clue.text: One making film about fringe members of monastic fraternity

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the outer letters of monastic are taken

parts.note: a religious order is a fraternity

explanation.surface: A documentary maker trailing the outlying brothers of a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringe members of' monastic gives MC.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld video recorder is a device that shoots footage.

clue.text: Character working to fix computer

indicators.note: fixing here means placing the computer inside

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a micro is a microcomputer

explanation.surface: A character working to repair a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a Greek letter, not a person; 'to fix' places the small machine inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter is a character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Pretty road, though uneven, in ancient city

indicators.note: the uneven, odd-numbered letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A pretty road, if bumpy, leads into an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' means odd: letters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 of PRETTYROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock-cut city in Jordan was capital of the Nabataeans in antiquity.

clue.text: Bland food with unpleasant odour, say? Add a strong-tasting spice

parts.note: pap is soft bland food

indicators.note: say signals the sound of the word for a smell

parts.note: a reek is a foul smell

explanation.surface: Bland food with a bad smell needs a spice added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives REEK by sound, spelt RIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground red pepper is a pungent seasoning.

clue.text: Words used in report predict Chinese collapse

indicators.note: the two words fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A forecast that the Chinese economy will fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported speech gives what someone said without quoting them, the grammar term for such wording.

clue.text: She is last to see monitor, way off

indicators.note: the final letter of see is taken
the way abbreviation is removed from the reptile

parts.note: a monitor is a large lizard
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A woman is the last to see the screen, as it is out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A monitor here is the lizard, not a screen; RD comes off it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, the female pronoun standing for any woman.

clue.text: Web-based story about transport?

indicators.note: about here signals the story being turned around

parts.note: an online story could be an e-tale

explanation.surface: An online story on the subject of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns E-TALE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to delight them, to fill them with joy.

clue.text: Piano composition son refused to hum

indicators.note: son is turned away, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: a song is a composition

explanation.surface: A son refusing to hum a piano piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' is a stink here, not singing; 'refused' takes the S from SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a bad smell.

clue.text: One that secured wife in divorce centre after going west?

indicators.note: the wife letter is placed within the reversed city
in an across answer going west means read right to left

parts.note: Reno, Nevada was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A man who kept hold of his wife despite heading west to a divorce town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns RENO into ONER, and W goes 'in'. Reno, Nevada, was where Americans went for quick divorces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has got hold of property holds title to it, the possessor.

clue.text: Unlikely to move in with a pal from Belfast?

parts.note: Belfast is in Northern Ireland, NI
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to budge, ensconced with an Irish friend.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland, whose capital is Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless will not stir, so it is unlikely to move.

clue.text: Welcome a vote about new sort of levy

indicators.note: the greeting word goes around the letter for new

parts.note: to greet someone is to welcome them
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A new environmental tax is welcomed by voters.
explanation.walkthrough: GREET 'about' N gives GREENT; A and X (a vote) follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge levied to discourage pollution is an eco-friendly type of tax.

clue.text: Hot news: British lost in battles at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the letter for British drops out of battles

explanation.surface: Breaking news: the British have been beaten in naval engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes B from BATTLES to leave ATTLES, which 'at sea' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent reports are the freshest, hot off the press.
